question: Should ClawSweeper adopt the release-train contract and six-class taxonomy proposed by https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/535 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106128 as a supported advisory CLI surface?
rationale: The patch can implement the proposed contract correctly, but code review cannot decide whether this governance model, metadata format, and repository path policy should become a maintained product contract.

options.title: Sponsor the advisory foundation
options.body: Approve the contract direction, request real shadow-run proof, and keep all publishing or enforcement work in later dependency-ordered PRs.

options.title: Defer pending policy validation
options.body: Keep the draft paused until the OpenClaw policy discussion and one manually evaluated release train establish a stable contract.

options.title: Decline the new control surface
options.body: Close the proposal if release scope should remain entirely within existing OpenClaw release procedures rather than ClawSweeper.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the advisory foundation
recommendation.body: Approve the contract direction, request real shadow-run proof, and keep all publishing or enforcement work in later dependency-ordered PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision affects repository-level release governance and ClawSweeper's supported automation boundary.
